claim: There are three job types you can use with an AWS Snowball Edge device, and every job follows the same workflow to order, receive and return devices.
question: How many job types does Snowball Edge have?

values.display: three job types
AWS Snowball Edge device

qualifiers.condition: import, export and local compute and storage jobs

evidence.quote: There are three job types you can use with an AWS Snowball Edge device.

claim: Each import job uses a single Snowball appliance: you copy the data to import into Amazon S3 onto the device, ship it back to AWS, and AWS imports the data into Amazon S3.
question: How does a Snowball Edge import job work?

values.display: Each import job uses a single Snowball appliance
we import your data into Amazon S3

evidence.quote: Each import job uses a single Snowball appliance. After you create a job to order a Snowball Edge device in the AWS Snow Family Management Console or the job management API, we ship a Snowball to you. When it arrives in a few days, you connect the Snowball Edge device to your network and transfer the data that you want imported into Amazon S3 onto the device. When you’re done transferring data, ship the Snowball back to AWS, and we import your data into Amazon S3.

claim: The import process cannot write from a Snow device to an S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock turned on with Default retention settings enabled, and it also cannot write if IAM policies on the bucket prevent writing.
question: When can a Snowball import not write to the S3 bucket?

values.display: S3 Object Lock and enabled Default retention settings
IAM policies on the bucket prevent writing

evidence.quote: The import process cannot write to buckets in Amazon S3 from the Snow device if you have turned on S3 Object Lock and enabled Default retention settings.
The import process also cannot write to your bucket in Amazon S3 if IAM policies on the bucket prevent writing to the bucket.

claim: Each export job can use any number of Snowball Edge devices; if the listing holds more data than fits on one device, several devices are provided, and each job part has exactly one device.
question: How many devices can a Snowball Edge export job use?

values.display: any number of AWS Snowball Edge devices
exactly one device associated with it

evidence.quote: Each export job can use any number of AWS Snowball Edge devices. If the listing contains more data than can fit on a single device, multiple devices are provided to you. Each job part has exactly one device associated with it.

claim: AWS Snowball Edge cannot export objects that are in the Amazon Glacier storage class; they must be restored before the export can succeed.
question: Can a Snowball Edge export job export objects stored in S3 Glacier?

values.display: cannot export objects that are in Amazon Glacier
must be restored

evidence.quote: It is important to note that AWS Snowball Edge cannot export objects that are in Amazon Glacier storage class. These objects must be restored before AWS Snowball Edge can successfully export the objects in the bucket.

claim: A Snowball Edge device provides local compute and storage by running EC2-compatible compute instances or Kubernetes containers in Amazon EKS Anywhere on Snow, with data stored in Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge.

evidence.quote: You can use the local compute and storage functionality of an AWS Snowball Edge device by running AWS EC2-compatible compute instances or Kubernetes containers in Amazon EKS Anywhere on Snow. For compute functionality, data storage is provided by Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge.

claim: When devices of a local compute and storage job are returned to AWS, all data stored in Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge is erased, and data stored in a cluster cannot be imported into Amazon S3 without ordering additional devices for separate import jobs.
question: Is data from a local compute and storage job imported into S3 when the device returns?

values.display: all data created or stored in Amazon S3
can't be imported into Amazon S3 without ordering

qualifiers.scope: Snowball Edge local compute and storage job and cluster

evidence.quote: When the device or devices are returned to AWS, all data created or stored in Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge is erased.
Like standalone local storage and compute jobs, the data stored in a cluster can't be imported into Amazon S3 without ordering additional devices as a part of separate import jobs.

claim: A cluster job is a special kind of job for local storage and compute only, for workloads that need more durability and capacity, and a cluster has 3 to 16 Snowball Edge devices called nodes.
question: What is a Snowball Edge cluster job?

values.display: 3 to 16 AWS Snowball Edge devices
special kind of job for local storage and

evidence.quote: A cluster job is a special kind of job for local storage and compute only. It is for those workloads that require increased data durability and storage capacity.
Clusters have 3 to 16 AWS Snowball Edge devices, called *nodes*.

claim: Regardless of the job type, every Snowball Edge job follows a data erasure of the NIST 800-88 standard after the job completes.
question: How is a Snowball Edge device sanitized after a job?

values.display: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-88 standard
every job follows a data erasure

evidence.quote: Regardless of the job type, every job follows a data erasure of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-88 standard after the job completes.

claim: When you import data with Snowball Edge, all data transferred to a device is protected by SSL encryption over the network, and Snowball Edge uses server-side encryption to protect data at rest; it supports SSE-S3.
question: How does Snowball Edge protect imported data in transit and at rest?

values.display: protected by SSL encryption over the network
supports server-side encryption with Amazon S3–managed encryption keys

evidence.quote: When you're using a Snowball Edge to import data into S3, all data transferred to a device is protected by SSL encryption over the network. To protect data at rest, AWS Snowball Edge uses server side-encryption (SSE).
AWS Snowball Edge supports server-side encryption with Amazon S3–managed encryption keys (SSE-S3).

claim: Currently AWS Snowball Edge does not offer server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C), although Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge offers SSE-C for local compute and storage jobs.
question: Does Snowball Edge offer SSE-C?

values.display: doesn't offer server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
offers SSE-C for local compute and storage jobs

evidence.quote: Currently, AWS Snowball Edge doesn't offer server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C). Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge offers SSE-C for local compute and storage jobs.

claim: In AWS Snowball Edge, AWS KMS protects the encryption keys used to protect data on each Snowball Edge device.

values.display: AWS KMS protects the encryption keys
data on each AWS Snowball Edge device

evidence.quote: In AWS Snowball Edge, AWS KMS protects the encryption keys used to protect data on each AWS Snowball Edge device.

claim: When you copy a file to Snowball Edge through the Amazon S3 interface, checksums are created to automatically validate data as it is transferred, and when the checksums do not match the associated data is not imported into Amazon S3.
question: What happens to a file whose checksum does not match on Snowball Edge?

values.display: checksums don't match
not imported into Amazon S3

evidence.quote: When you copy a file from a local data source using the Amazon S3 interface to the Snowball Edge, a number of checksums are created. These checksums are used to automatically validate data as it's transferred.
When these checksums don't match, the associated data is not imported into Amazon S3.

claim: Data transferred through the Snowball Edge NFS interface is not encrypted in transit, although you can provide CIDR blocks to restrict which clients can access the interface.
question: Is data copied over the Snowball Edge NFS interface encrypted in transit?

values.display: not encrypted in transit
provide CIDR blocks

evidence.quote: Data transferred through the NFS interface is not encrypted in transit. When configuring the NFS interface, you can provide CIDR blocks and the Snowball Edge will restrict access to the NFS interface from client computers with addresses in those blocks.

claim: The Snowball Edge NFS interface is available for import jobs, and you can use it if the device was configured to include it when the job to order the device was created; otherwise use the S3 adapter or Amazon S3 compatible storage.

configured to include it when the job to

evidence.quote: The NFS interface is available for import jobs.
You can use the NFS interface if the Snowball Edge device was configured to include it when the job to order the device was created.

claim: Each copy operation to Snowball Edge has overhead because of encryption, so to speed up transferring small files you can batch them together in a single archive that can be auto-extracted when imported into Amazon S3.
question: How do you speed up copying many small files to Snowball Edge?

values.display: batch them together in a single archive
overhead because of encryption

qualifiers.condition: batches larger than 100 GB are not extracted on import

evidence.quote: Each copy operation has some overhead because of encryption. To speed up the process of transferring small files to your AWS Snowball Edge device, you can batch them together in a single archive. When you batch files together, they can be auto-extracted when they are imported into Amazon S3, if they were batched in one of the supported archive formats.

claim: The Snowball Edge manifest authenticates your access to the device and is encrypted so that only the unlock code can decrypt it; AWS recommends keeping the unlock code separate from the manifest.
question: What do the manifest and unlock code do on a Snowball Edge device?

values.display: only the unlock code can decrypt it
authenticate your access to the device

evidence.quote: The manifest is used to authenticate your access to the device, and it is encrypted so that only the unlock code can decrypt it. You can get the manifest from the console or with the job management API when the device is on-premises at your location.
We recommend that you keep the unlock code saved somewhere separate from the manifest to prevent unauthorized access to the device while it’s at your facility.
